extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates, graduate students, and researchers learning or using algebraic topology (homotopy theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria and definitions from a textbook chapter on homotopy groups, CW complexes, Postnikov/Moore–Postnikov towers, cellular approximation, and obstruction theory; intended to guide correct definitions, constructions, and verification steps in homotopy-theoretic arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of homotopy groups πn(X, x0)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a space X with basepoint x0, πn(X, x0) is the set of homotopy classes of maps f : (In, ∂In) → (X, x0), with homotopies required to satisfy ft(∂In) = x0 for all t. The definition extends to n = 0 by taking I0 a point and ∂I0 empty, so π0(X, x0) is the set of path-components of X. Equivalently πn(X, x0) are homotopy classes of basepoint-preserving maps (S^n, s0) → (X, x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational definition; maps may be interpreted via quotient In/∂In = S^n. The definition for n = 0 yields components; for n ≥ 1 homotopies fix the boundary. Use the S^n viewpoint when convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group structure on πn
rubrics_metrics.description: For n ≥ 1 a sum operation is defined (e.g. using the first coordinate) making πn(X, x0) a group; identity is the constant map and inverses are given by reversing the first coordinate. For n ≥ 2 the group πn(X, x0) is abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sum is defined by splitting In into two halves in the first coordinate and using the same arguments as for π1 to show group axioms. Commutativity for n ≥ 2 is shown by a homotopy that shrinks supports to subcubes and slides them past each other (requires at least two coordinates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basepoint-change isomorphism and π1-action on πn
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a path γ from x0 to x1, there is a change-of-basepoint isomorphism βγ : πn(X, x1) → πn(X, x0) defined by βγ([f]) = [γ f]. For loops at the basepoint this yields a homomorphism π1(X, x0) → Aut(πn(X, x0)), i.e. an action of π1 on πn. Elements of Z[π1] act on πn making πn a Z[π1]-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties recorded: (1) γ(f+g) ≃ γf + γg, (2) (γη)f ≃ γ(ηf), (3) 1f ≃ f. When n = 1 the action is by inner automorphisms; when n > 1 the action equips πn with module structure. Spaces with trivial π1-action on πn are called 'n-simple'; 'simple' means trivial action for all n. The book uses 'abelian' to mean trivial action on all homotopy groups (consistent with π1 abelian when n = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality of πn
rubrics_metrics.description: A map ϕ : (X, x0) → (Y, y0) induces ϕ* : πn(X, x0) → πn(Y, y0) by ϕ*([f]) = [ϕ f]. If ϕt is a homotopy then ϕ0* = ϕ1*. Homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms on all πn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard functoriality is used throughout: composing maps corresponds to composing induced maps on homotopy groups; homotopic maps induce the same map on homotopy groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of πn with respect to covering spaces (Proposition 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p : (aX, a x0) → (X, x0) is a covering space projection, then p* : πn(a X, a x0) → πn(X, x0) is an isomorphism for all n ≥ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surjectivity follows from lifting criterion (S^n simply-connected for n ≥ 2); injectivity from the covering homotopy property. Consequence: if X has contractible universal cover then πn(X) = 0 for n ≥ 2 (aspherical spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of πn with respect to products (Proposition 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a product Q_α X_α of an arbitrary collection of path-connected spaces, πn(Q_α X_α) ≈ Q_α πn(X_α) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A map from Y into the product corresponds to a collection of maps into the factors; take Y = S^n or S^n × I to prove statements about πn and homotopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of relative homotopy groups πn(X, A, x0)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a pair (X, A) with basepoint x0 ∈ A, πn(X, A, x0) (n ≥ 1) is the set of homotopy classes of maps (In, ∂In, J_{n-1}) → (X, A, x0) (equivalently (Dn, S^{n-1}, s0) → (X, A, x0)). πn(X, A, x0) is a group for n ≥ 2 and abelian for n ≥ 3. For n = 1 it is the set of homotopy classes of paths in X from a varying point in A to x0 and generally not a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition is defined via collapsing maps Dn → Dn ∨ Dn as in the absolute case. Relative groups generalize absolute groups since πn(X, x0, x0) = πn(X, x0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression criterion for triviality in πn(X, A, x0)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f : (Dn, S^{n-1}, s0) → (X, A, x0) represents zero in πn(X, A, x0) iff it is homotopic rel S^{n-1} to a map with image contained in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a homotopy to g exists then [f] = [g] and [g] = 0 via composing with a deformation retraction of Dn to s0. Conversely, a nullhomotopy yields such a homotopy by restricting to a family of disks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence of a pair and triple (Theorem 4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a long exact sequence ... → πn(A, x0) i*→ πn(X, x0) j*→ πn(X, A, x0) ∂→ π_{n-1}(A, x0) → ··· → π0(X, x0). Similarly for triples (X, A, B, x0). The boundary map ∂ is obtained by restriction to the face In−1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exactness means image equals kernel at each stage; near π0 where group structures may not exist exactness is interpreted as elements mapping to the homotopy class of the constant map. The proof uses the compression criterion and homotopy extension arguments; naturality holds for maps of triples.

rubrics_metrics.name: n-connectedness (absolute and relative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A space X is n-connected if πi(X, x0) = 0 for i ≤ n (0-connected = path-connected, 1-connected = simply-connected). Equivalent formulations: (1) every map S^i → X is nullhomotopic for i ≤ n; (2) every map S^i → X extends to D^{i+1}; (3) πi(X, x0) = 0 for all x0. For pairs (X, A) similar equivalent conditions (maps (D^i, ∂D^i) → (X, A) homotopic rel ∂ to maps into A, etc.) define n-connected pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pairs the condition for i = 0 is that each path-component of X contains points of A. These equivalent formulations are practical tests for connectivity in constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitehead's Theorem (Theorem 4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a map f : X → Y between connected CW complexes induces isomorphisms f* : πn(X) → πn(Y) for all n, then f is a homotopy equivalence. If f is the inclusion of a subcomplex, then X is a deformation retract of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to vanishing of relative groups and uses the compression lemma and mapping cylinder arguments; note the hypothesis requires a map inducing the isomorphisms, not merely isomorphic groups abstractly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression lemma (Lemma 4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (X, A) be a CW pair and (Y, B) any pair with B ≠ ∅. For each n such that X − A has cells of dimension n, assume πn(Y, B, y0) = 0 for all y0 ∈ B. Then every map f : (X, A) → (Y, B) is homotopic rel A to a map X → B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by induction on skeleta: deform characteristic maps of cells into B using hypothesis; extend homotopies by homotopy extension property. Use iterative homotopies on shrinking time intervals to handle infinitely many cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension lemma (Lemma 4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a CW pair (X, A) and a map f : A → Y with Y path-connected, f can be extended to a map X → Y if π_{n-1}(Y) = 0 for all n such that X − A has cells of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inductive extension over skeleta: an extension over an n-cell exists iff the attaching map S^{n-1} → X^{n-1} composed with f is nullhomotopic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular approximation theorem (Theorem 4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every map f : X → Y of CW complexes is homotopic to a cellular map (one sending X^n into Y^n for all n). If f is cellular on a subcomplex A ⊂ X, the homotopy may be taken stationary on A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses local compactness to ensure images meet only finitely many cells, then iteratively deforms maps on cells to miss higher-dimensional cells using PL approximations and local homotopies; handles infinitely many cells by arranging homotopies on shrinking t-intervals. Corollary: πn(S^k) = 0 for n < k by cellular approximation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular approximation for pairs and connectivity corollary (Example 4.11, Corollary 4.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every map f : (X, A) → (Y, B) of CW pairs can be deformed through maps of pairs to a cellular map. If all cells in X − A have dimension > n then (X, A) is n-connected. In particular (X, X^n) is n-connected, so inclusion X^n ↪ X induces isomorphisms on πi for i < n and a surjection on πn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cellular approximation applied first to A→B then extend to X and reapply to get cellular maps fixed on A.

rubrics_metrics.name: CW approximation existence and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: For every space X there exists a CW complex Z and a weak homotopy equivalence f : Z → X (i.e. induces isomorphisms on πn for all n and basepoints). Such a CW approximation is unique up to homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction is inductive: attach cells to kill kernels and make maps surjective on πi in stages so that at stage k, f*: π_{k-1}(B)→π_{k-1}(X) is injective and f*: π_k(B)→π_k(X) is surjective. Uniqueness follows because two approximations map into a common mapping cylinder and compression lemma gives homotopy equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eilenberg–MacLane spaces K(G, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW complex with a single nontrivial homotopy group (πn ≈ G, other πi = 0) is an Eilenberg–MacLane space K(G,n). Cohomology classes in a CW complex correspond bijectively with homotopy classes of maps from the complex into an Eilenberg–MacLane space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K(G,n) characterize cohomology: [X, K(G,n)] ≈ H^n(X; G). K(G,n) appear as fibers/stages in Postnikov towers and are central to obstruction theory. Construction of K(G,n) often proceeds by attaching cells of dimension ≥ n+2 to S^n (exercise remark).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freudenthal suspension theorem / stability of homotopy groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Along each diagonal the groups π_{n+k}(S^n) with k fixed and varying n eventually become independent of n for large enough n (stability property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the origin of stable homotopy groups; proved in the following section (§4.2). It underlies the study of stable phenomena and motivates the Freudenthal suspension theorem and stable homotopy groups of spheres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurewicz theorem (statement and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a simply-connected space X, the first nonzero homotopy group π_n(X) is isomorphic to the first nonzero homology group H_n(X). There is a relative version as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to explain the diagonal Z's in homotopy groups of spheres table and to relate homotopy-theoretic information to homology; a cornerstone linking homotopy and homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postnikov and Moore–Postnikov towers (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Moore–Postnikov tower for f : X → Y is a diagram X → ... → Z_n → Z_{n-1} → ... → Z_1 → Y such that: (1) X → Z_n induces isomorphism on π_i for i < n and surjection for i = n; (2) Z_n → Y induces isomorphism on π_i for i > n and injection for i = n; (3) Z_{n+1} → Z_n is a fibration with fiber K(π_n F, n) where F is the homotopy fiber of f. A Postnikov tower is the special case with Y a point (gives stages X_n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Towers factor maps into successive principal fibrations with Eilenberg–MacLane fibers; they are central to obstruction-theoretic and classification arguments. One may replace maps by homotopy-equivalent fibrations to make triangles strictly commutative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of Moore–Postnikov towers and principal fibration condition (Theorem 4.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every map f : X → Y between connected CW complexes has a Moore–Postnikov tower, unique up to homotopy equivalence. A tower of principal fibrations exists iff π1(X) acts trivially on πn(Mf, X) for all n > 1, where Mf is the mapping cylinder of f. The fibers of successive maps Zn+1 → Zn are Eilenberg–MacLane spaces K(π_{n}F, n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: apply Propositions 4.17 and 4.18 to (Mf, X) and then replace maps by fibrations; use homotopy lifting to strictify commutativity. Principal fibration condition ties to trivial π1-actions and Lemma 4.70.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obstruction theory: extension and relative lifting problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a CW pair (W, A) and map A → X (extension problem) or a fibration X → Y and W → Y with lift on A (relative lifting problem), one can attempt to lift/extend stagewise through a (Moore–)Postnikov tower. At the nth stage the obstruction to lifting lies in a cohomology class ω_n ∈ H^{n+1}(W, A; π_n X) (or with coefficients π_n F for lifting problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 4.72: a lift W → X_n extending given A → X_n exists iff ω_n = 0. The obstruction is obtained by regarding W ∪ CA → K(π_n X, n+1) and asking whether this map is nullhomotopic (equivalently whether the cohomology class vanishes). Choices of lifts at earlier stages can change later obstructions; well-defined primary obstructions occur when π_i(F) = 0 for i < n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary on vanishing cohomology implying extendability (Corollary 4.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a connected abelian CW complex and (W, A) is a CW pair such that H^{n+1}(W, A; π_n X) = 0 for all n, then every map A → X can be extended to W → X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a direct application of obstruction-theoretic vanishing of all stage obstructions; abelian hypothesis (trivial π1-action) ensures obstructions live in ordinary cohomology groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology equivalence implies homotopy equivalence for abelian CW complexes (Proposition 4.74)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are connected abelian CW complexes, a map f : X → Y inducing isomorphisms on all homology groups is a homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: reduce to inclusion case via mapping cylinder. Use relative Hurewicz theorem and obstruction theory to construct a retraction Y → X (no obstructions because H_*(Y, X) = 0), deducing weak homotopy equivalence and hence homotopy equivalence for CW complexes.
